title: Anything With Geometry — Ink on Paper: the Pen-Plotter Loop
thesis: Fogleman's ln turns any 3D scene into hidden-line vector paths, and vpype makes those paths plotter-ready. Everything else in the catalog that produces geometry — a phone scan, a ripped PS1 level, a ray-marched fractal, a strange attractor, the phase-space shape of BTC volatility, a Blender scene an agent wrote in Python — becomes a source for that one pipe. The output is a physical ink original, and in a market drowning in free pixels that is the scarce thing.
why_it_matters: You get a repeatable way to make signed physical editions from subjects nobody else is drawing, with the agent doing the scene work and the plotter doing the craft. Print-on-demand and no-proposal grants already give you a path to sell and fund it.

Falsifier: if scanned or ripped meshes produce unreadable line mush unless you hand-pick every path, or if plotted originals cannot sell above the POD print price, the loop is a toy, not a practice

entries.transcript: Today's open source project is LN, the 3D lineart engine. These scenes are 3D, but the output isn't pixels, it's lines. It's by Michael Fogelman, written in Go. He made it so he could plot 3D drawings with his pen plotter. An OpenGL pipeline gives you a raster image. LN gives you 2D vector paths. Every shape is covered in 3D paths. LN chops them into tiny pieces, and from each point shoots a ray toward the camera. If nothing is hit, the point is visible. If something is in the way, it's hidden and never drawn. So the texture is just the paths you choose. Over-eyed paths and a cube become stripes. It also does solid geometry. A sphere trimmed by a cube and drilled by three cylinders. Math functions become surfaces, random walks become strings of beads, and random boxes become a city. Before plotting, there's V-pipe by Antoine Baylor, a Swiss army knife for plotter graphics. Here, line merge and line sort cut the pen up travel by 86%. For visual work, render a scene straight to SVG. Plot it in real ink, or turn a moving camera into a line animation. Both are MIT licensed. Thank you. Bye.

entries.caption:
Can one line of math build an entire 3D world? This is the Mandelbulb, and it comes from z ↦ z⁸ + c.

In 2D, the Mandelbrot set repeats z ↦ z² + c: pick a point c, start at zero, square, add c, repeat. If it never escapes past |z| = 2, the point is black. Squaring a complex number squares its length and doubles its angle.

There is no such multiplication for points in 3D. William Rowan Hamilton tried for years; in an 1865 letter he remembers his sons asking every morning, "Well, Papa, can you multiply triplets?" and his answer, "No, I can only add and subtract them." Daniel White's 2007 idea was to copy the geometry in spherical coordinates, and Paul Nylander raised it to the 8th power: r ↦
entries.transcript: This one line of math builds an entire world. It runs inside Mandelbulb, an open source program that flies a camera through fractals. It all starts flat, with the Mandelbrot set. Pick a point C, start at zero, square it, add C, and repeat. If it never runs away, paint it black. And squaring hides a trick. The length gets squared, and the angle doubles. In three dimensions, numbers like that do not exist. William Hamilton spent years trying to multiply triplets. Every morning his sons asked, well Papa, can you multiply triplets? And he always answered, no, I can only add and subtract them. So Daniel White just copied the geometry, and Paul Milander pushed it further. Raise the length to the eighth power, and multiply both angles by eight. At power two, it's a lumpy blob. At power eight, it blooms, with bumps on bumps all the way down. To draw it, every pixel shoots a ray. The formula says how close the surface could be. So the ray jumps exactly that far, and asks again. This one needed thirteen jumps. One frame of this video takes eight million rays, a hundred million jumps, and three hundred million turns of that one line. And all of it comes from one line.

title: Strategy Autoresearch — the judge is the product, not the agent
thesis: Self-rewriting loops (Karpathy-style autoresearch, bilevel coach loops, Microsoft SkillOpt) keep any edit that beats a benchmark. Point one at trading and it becomes an industrial overfitting machine — the backtest is the benchmark, and the loop will beat it ten thousand times. The quant saves already hold the fix: probability of backtest overfitting, permutation tests, transaction costs and backtest-to-live drift. Wire those in as the loop's judge, and use the loop's own log as the exact count of trials — the number human quants never know.
why_it_matters: A solo builder can run more strategy variants in a weekend than a small fund tests in a quarter. The difference between that being an edge and a casino is whether the gate deflates for every attempt. Most likely you learn you have no edge, cheaply, and that's worth money too.
action_sketch:
Wrap a vectorized backtester (VectorBT) in a SkillOpt-style loop where Claude proposes strategy edits and every proposal is appended to a trials table with its parameters and result.
Replace 'beats benchmark' with a judge that needs all four: positive after realistic fees, beats 95% of a permutation null, deflated Sharpe positive using the trials-table count, and a held-out year scored once at the end.
Have a second model (Codex or GPT) audit each surviving strategy's code for look-ahead bias before it reaches paper trading; monitor live drift with Wasserstein distance and auto-retire on breach.
falsifier: seed the loop with pure-noise synthetic prices. If anything passes the judge, the judge is broken — fix it before you show it a real market.
prerequisites: Python and VectorBT or similar backtester
Clean historical data with realistic cost assumptions
Discipline to treat 'no survivors' as a valid result

thesis: OpenAI built a $230 hardware controller for babysitting coding agents. entries.transcript: This is a Sharp memory display. At first glance, it looks just like another tiny LCD, but it's actually a completely different kind of screen. A normal LCD has to constantly refresh the image, redrawing the entire display over and over again even if nothing changes. That's fine for phones and monitors, but it wastes a surprising amount of power. Our Sharp memory display works differently. Every pixel stores its own state, so once you draw something, it simply stays there. It's very similar to an e-paper screen. The display only needs a tiny maintenance signal in the background which makes it incredibly power efficient. Another thing I love is that it's reflective instead of backlit. So the brighter it is outside, the easier it is to read. Playdate, for example, uses a Sharp memory display and can run it up to 50 frames per second. That makes it a really interesting middle ground. You can get fast updates like a normal LCD, excellent outdoor visibility like e-paper, and low power consumption whenever the image is mostly static. It's a really clever display.

A single shepherd dog can control an entire flock of sheep without ever touching them. The secret is spatial pressure — the exploitation of every prey animal's flight zone.
When a predator (or herding dog) enters the flight zone — the minimum distance at which an animal perceives a threat — the animal moves away. The dog does not chase individual sheep. Instead, it positions itself behind the flock relative to the target destination. This creates a directional pressure wave that pushes the entire group forward.

Everything inside that circle moves away from the dog. A wider radius means the dog controls more sheep at once. Total flock control. Shrink the radius and the dog must chase harder. The sheep scatter in every direction. Cohesion is the glue holding the flock together. It determines how tightly they pack. High cohesion and the flock moves as a single dense ball. One unit easy to herd. Low cohesion and individuals break away. Total chaos for the dog. Stubborn sheep resist the dog's pressure. They refuse to flee as easily. Maximum stubbornness and sheep plant their feet. They barely move even when pressured. Zero stubbornness and they are completely docile. The dog herds them effortlessly. Now a faster dog.
